src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test GS-MA 201
s: The newly formed Andhra Pradesh has to depend mainly on resources like
Under UNCLOS, in which zone does full sovereignty, subject to innocent passage, apply?
x: The territorial sea (12 nm) gives full sovereignty subject to innocent passage; the high seas carry freedom of navigation.

s: The Exclusive Economic Zone extends up to how many nautical miles from the baseline?
x: The EEZ extends to 200 nautical miles, where the coastal state has sovereign rights over living and non-living resources.

s: In which year was India's domestic law on maritime zones (territorial waters, continental shelf and EEZ) enacted?
x: The Territorial Waters, Continental Shelf, EEZ and Other Maritime Zones Act was passed in 1976. 1982 and 1994 are when UNCLOS was adopted and came into force; 1956 is unrelated.

s: What is the world rank of India's Exclusive Economic Zone of about 2.37 million sq km?
x: India's EEZ of about 2.37 million sq km is the world's 18th largest, much of it added by the Andaman-Nicobar and Lakshadweep islands.

s: In which year was the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) adopted?
x: UNCLOS was adopted in 1982 and came into force in 1994; it set up the International Seabed Authority.

s: Under UNCLOS, the contiguous zone extends up to how far from the baseline?
x: The contiguous zone reaches 24 nm; the territorial sea is 12 nm and the EEZ 200 nm.

s: Up to what distance can a coastal state's continental shelf extend?
x: The continental shelf (seabed and subsoil) can extend up to 350 nm.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about UNCLOS maritime zones?
o: Contiguous zone – Customs and immigration laws
x: In the EEZ the coastal state has only sovereign rights over resources; full sovereignty applies in the 12 nm territorial sea.

s: Which body, set up under UNCLOS, grants contracts for exploring seabed minerals in international waters?
x: UNCLOS set up the International Seabed Authority (ISA), which licenses seabed exploration such as India's nodule and sulphide contracts.

s: In which year did UNCLOS come into force?
x: UNCLOS was adopted in 1982 and came into force in 1994; it set up the International Seabed Authority.

s: What are gas hydrates?
o: Methane ice occurring in seabed sediments
x: Gas hydrates are methane ice deposits occurring in seabed sediments.

s: What are seabed deposits carrying copper, zinc, lead and iron along with silver, gold and platinum called?
x: Polymetallic sulphides carry copper, zinc, lead, iron, silver, gold and platinum; polymetallic nodules contain nickel, copper, cobalt and manganese.

s: In which year did India become the first Pioneer Investor in the Central Indian Ocean Basin?
x: India became the first Pioneer Investor in the Central Indian Ocean Basin in 1987.

s: Which of the following pairs (India's ISA contract – year) is correctly matched?
o: Polymetallic nodules, Central Indian Ocean Basin – 2016
Polymetallic nodules, Central Indian Ocean Basin – 15 September 2025
Polymetallic sulphides, Central and South West Indian Ridge – 2016
x: The Central and South West Indian Ridge sulphide contract dates to 2016; the CIOB nodule contract is from 2002 and the Carlsberg Ridge sulphide contract from 15 September 2025.

s: Which metals do the polymetallic nodules of the Central Indian Ocean Basin mainly carry?
x: Polymetallic nodules carry nickel, copper, cobalt and manganese; monazite and ilmenite are beach placers and gas hydrates are methane ice.

s: Which area does India's third ISA contract (15 September 2025), for polymetallic sulphides, cover?
o: Central and South West Indian Ridge
x: Contract 3 (2025) is for sulphides on the Carlsberg Ridge; Contract 2 (2016) covered the Central and South West Indian Ridge.

s: In which of the following basins are gas hydrates, the methane ice of seabed sediments, being explored under the National Gas Hydrate Programme?
x: Gas hydrates are explored in the Krishna-Godavari, Mahanadi and Andaman areas under the National Gas Hydrate Programme.

s: For beach placers of which minerals are Chavara, Manavalakurichi and Chatrapur known?
x: Chavara (Kerala), Manavalakurichi (Tamil Nadu), Chatrapur (Odisha) and the Andhra coast have monazite (thorium) and ilmenite (titanium) beach placers.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Mumbai High — Western offshore oil and gas basin
x: Chavara is known for beach placer minerals, especially monazite and ilmenite, not as an offshore petroleum basin. Mumbai High, Krishna-Godavari and Cauvery are oil and gas basins.

s: Which is the nodal ministry for India's Deep Ocean Mission?
o: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying
x: The Deep Ocean Mission (approved June 2021, ₹4,077 crore) is run by the Ministry of Earth Sciences, not the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Deep Ocean Mission?
o: It is one of the nine PM-STIAC missions.
Its focus areas include deep-sea mining and a manned submersible.
It excludes ocean energy and freshwater-related activities.
Ocean biodiversity and ocean survey are among its focus areas.
x: Ocean energy and freshwater are also among the mission's focus areas, so saying it excludes them is false; the other three are correct.

s: How many offshore mineral blocks were in the first tranche auctioned under a composite licence (November 2024)?
x: The first tranche, auctioned on 28 November 2024 under the OAMDR Act, had 13 offshore blocks.

s: The Draft Blue Economy Policy Framework was prepared by which ministry in 2021?
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
x: The Draft Blue Economy Policy Framework, 2021, is associated with the Ministry of Earth Sciences.

s: Samudrayaan's submersible Matsya 6000 is designed to carry how many crew to 6,000 m?
x: Matsya 6000 is an indigenous submersible for 3 crew to 6,000 m.

s: What is the outlay of the Deep Ocean Mission, approved in June 2021 for 5 years?
x: The Deep Ocean Mission (MoES) was approved with ₹4,077 crore for 5 years.

s: Of which element is monazite, found in beach placers, an ore?
x: Monazite yields thorium; ilmenite yields titanium.

s: Which of the following is an oil and gas basin of India?
x: Mumbai High is an oil and gas basin; Chavara, Manavalakurichi and Chatrapur are beach placer sites.

s: Ilmenite, found in the beach placers of Chavara and Manavalakurichi, is an ore of which metal?
x: Ilmenite is an ore of titanium; monazite from the same placers gives thorium.

Which of the following country is the largest producer of pearls?
x: Japan is recognized as the world's largest producer and trader of cultured pearls, owing to its long history of pearl cultivation pioneered by Kokichi Mikimoto.

s: The north-west Pacific fishing ground is associated with the meeting of which currents?
x: The north-west Pacific fishing ground lies where the Kuroshio and Oyashio meet; the Gulf Stream-Labrador meeting is the Grand Banks.

s: Which of the following favours the development of major fishing grounds?
o: Highly arid interiors with no coastal access
Mixing of warm and cold currents
x: Wide shallow shelves, mixing of warm and cold currents, upwelling and indented coasts favour fishing grounds.

s: Which country among the following is identified as having exports that lean most heavily on fish?
x: Norway, Japan and Iceland are fishing-dependent countries, but Iceland's exports lean most heavily on fish.

s: Off which place does the Grand Banks fishing ground lie?
x: The Grand Banks lie off Newfoundland in the NW Atlantic, where the Gulf Stream meets the Labrador Current.

s: In which sea does Dogger Bank, a shallow sandbank fishing ground, lie?
x: Dogger Bank is a shallow sandbank in the North Sea, about 100 km off eastern England.

s:
Consider the following statements about pearl production:
1. Japan is the classic largest producer of cultured Akoya pearls.
2. By volume, China now leads.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: Japan is the classic producer of cultured Akoya pearls, while China now leads by volume.

src: APPSC 2018 Question Papers and Keys for Mains Exams
s: The national fish of India is
x: Indian Mackerel is the commonly cited national fish of India, though not formally notified. Pomfret, Hilsa and Rohu are not given this status in the notes (Golden Mahseer is sometimes cited, but it is not among the options).

s: Which of the following is associated with “Blue Revolution”?
x: The Blue Revolution refers to the remarkable emergence of aquaculture. Aquaculture refers to all form of active culturing of aquatic animals, plants and fishes. It is not related to poultry. Thus, it is not correctly matched. All other options are correctly matched.

s: The ‘Blue Revolution’ is associated with
x: The Blue Revolution refers to the remarkable emergence of aquaculture. Aquaculture refers to all form of active culturing of aquatic animals, plants and fishes. It is not related to poultry. Thus, it is not correctly matched. All other options are correctly matched.

s: The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (2020) comes under which ministry?
o: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying
x: PMMSY, the Blue Revolution flagship, is under the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying; the Ministry of Earth Sciences runs the Deep Ocean Mission.

s: What is India's current rank among the world's fish producers?
o: third-largest fish producer, after Japan and China
largest fish producer, ahead of China
fourth-largest fish producer, after Norway, China and Japan
x: India is the second-largest fish producer after China and contributes approximately 8–9% of global output.

s: The annual mechanised fishing ban in India's territorial waters lasts how many days?
x: Territorial-water fisheries (0-12 nm) are a State subject, with an annual two-month (61-day) ban on mechanised fishing.

s: Inland fisheries contribute about what share of India's fish production?
x: Inland fisheries contribute more than 75% of India's fish production.

s: How is the Access Pass for vessels of 24 m or more issued under the EEZ Rules, 2025?
o: Through ReALCraft on payment of a fee
x: The Access Pass, mandatory for mechanised and motorised vessels of at least 24 m, is issued through ReALCraft at zero fee; traditional crafts are exempt.

s: In India's territorial waters (0–12 nm), what kind of subject are fisheries?
x: Fisheries within 0–12 nm are a State subject; 12–200 nm comes under the Centre.

s: What is the subsidy under PMMSY for women, SC and ST beneficiaries?
x: PMMSY gives 40% subsidy to general beneficiaries and 60% to women, SC and ST.

s: Which is the national aquatic animal of India?
x: The Gangetic dolphin is India's national aquatic animal; the Indian Mackerel is cited as the national fish.

s: Which item leads India's seafood exports?
x: India's seafood exports (₹62,408 crore in FY 2024-25) are led by frozen shrimp.

s: With which sector is the Blue Revolution associated?
x: The Blue Revolution refers to the growth of fisheries and aquaculture.

s: The term "Blue economy" refers to
What is the blue economy?
o: Exclusive commercial use of deep-sea minerals
Replacement of all terrestrial economic activities by maritime trade
Use of coastal waters only for naval security
Sustainable use of ocean, coastal and inland waters for growth, jobs and conservation
x: The blue economy involves sustainable use of ocean, coastal and inland waters to promote economic growth, employment and conservation.

s: What does SAGAR, the Indian Ocean vision articulated by the Prime Minister in 2015, stand for?
o: Sustainable Alliance for Global Aquatic Resources
Security and Governance of All Regional Waters
Strategic Agreement for Governance of Asian Routes
Security and Growth for All in the Region
x: SAGAR means “Security and Growth for All in the Region.” It was articulated as India's Indian Ocean vision in 2015 at Mauritius.

s: In which country did the Prime Minister articulate the SAGAR vision in 2015?
x: SAGAR ('Security and Growth for All in the Region') was articulated in Mauritius in 2015.

s: 'Blue Economy' is related with
Which one of the following is an aquaculture district of Andhra Pradesh?
x: West Godavari is among the listed aquaculture districts, along with Eluru, Krishna, Bapatla, Nellore, Konaseema and Kakinada.

s: Under which programme are 10 fishing harbours being built in Andhra Pradesh?
x: The 10 fishing harbours are being constructed under PMMSY, not Sagarmala.

s: Where is the Centre of Excellence on Blue Economy in Andhra Pradesh located?
x: The Centre of Excellence on Blue Economy is located at Vignan's University, Vadlamudi, in Guntur.

s: Andhra Pradesh accounts for about what share of India's fish production?
x: Andhra Pradesh produces about 30% of India's fish and 31% of its shrimp exports.

s: In which basin do Andhra Pradesh's offshore oil and gas mainly lie?
x: AP's oil and gas are in the Krishna-Godavari (KG) basin.

s: Which shrimp species dominates Andhra Pradesh's shrimp exports?
x: AP accounts for about 31% of India's shrimp exports, mainly of the Vannamei shrimp.

s: Along which coast of Andhra Pradesh are beach sand minerals found?
x: AP's beach sand minerals lie along the Srikakulam–Bhimunipatnam coast; its oil and gas lie in the KG basin.
